# introduction
This document records my learning process in R Markdown.
## Loading Required Packages
We will install and load the necessary packages.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```
rmarkdown
```{R}
# Install required packages if not already installed
if (!require("tidyverse")) install.packages("tidyverse")
if (!require("airway")) BiocManager::install("airway")

# Load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(airway)
library(DT)
```

## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r}
# Summarize the built-in cars dataset
summary(cars)
```
## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:
```{r}
# Plot the built-in pressure dataset
plot(pressure)
```


Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
- The **backticks `{r}`** tell R Markdown that this is R code.
- The code inside runs when you **knit** the document.

## Data Analysis in R
Let's explore some built-in datasets in R.

### Summary of the `cars` dataset:
```{r summarize-cars}
summary(cars)
```

```{r}
plot(pressure)

```



r
### Interpretation of the `cars` dataset summary:
The `summary(cars)` function provides the minimum, maximum, median, mean, and quartiles for the `speed` and `dist` columns in the dataset.
### Interpretation of the `pressure` dataset plot:
The plot generated by `plot(pressure)` shows the relationship between temperature and pressure. It helps visualize how pressure changes with temperature.
## Conclusion
In this assignment, I have learned how to use R Markdown to embed R code, perform basic data analysis, and visualize results. I also explored the `cars` and `pressure` datasets, which helped me understand how to summarize and plot data in R.
